_comment: Guided tour of the mean micro-time tool in the emtk window. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to use them.

steps.title: What this tool computes
steps.text: For every detector window the photon-weighted mean arrival time of each pixel, in nanoseconds, plus the intensity. It is not a fitted lifetime: it is the first moment of the micro-time histogram, offset by the electronics delay. You press the buttons; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Choose the photon file
steps.text: A PTU or HT3 file with line and frame markers. Type a path and press Enter, press Browse or Database, or drop a file on the window.

await.hint: Select a photon file. Nothing is computed until you press Run.

steps.title: Minimum photons
steps.text: A mean of a few photons is noise. Pixels with fewer photons than this are discriminated and set to 0 (and drawn as the lowest colour). Changing it needs a new Run.

steps.title: Compute
steps.text: Run reads the photons and fills one set of maps per detector window in the background; the Detectors tab is the Setup tool's editor for the windows.

await.hint: Press Run and wait until the status line is empty.

steps.title: The mean micro-time map
steps.text: Short mean times (dark) are quenched or fast-decaying regions, long ones slow decays. Compare it with the intensity: a dim pixel may have a perfectly good lifetime.

steps.title: The movie
steps.text: The same estimate for each scanner frame, played as a movie; it shows whether the lifetime changes during the acquisition.

steps.title: Write the result
steps.text: Add mean micro-time to HDF5 appends the columns to the pipeline's imaging HDF5 (or asks for a file); Save container, ndX and Next work as in the other per-pixel tools.

await.hint: Press Add mean micro-time to HDF5 and choose a file name.
